Group1: both entry and exit null. Expect Objects.hash(null,null) == 961. We need to compute that value; but we can just assert that hashCode equals Objects.hash(null,null). Compute expected value maybe 961 as given. We'll assert equals 961.

Group2: entry non-null, exit null. entry hashCode == 10 (they claim). Need to mock Trade to have hashCode 10. Use Mockito to create mock Trade with hashCode returning 10. Then Position with entry mock and exit null. Expected hash code 1271. Compute Objects.hash(entry, null) should equal 1271 given entry hash 10.

Group3: entry hashCode throws RuntimeException. Use mock Trade where hashCode throws RuntimeException. When calling Position.hashCode, expect exception.

We need to add these tests to class Position_hashCode_Test, respecting existing @BeforeEach etc. We can add new test methods. Use MockitoExtension already.

We need to import java.util.Objects maybe.

In existing tests they used new Position(entryBuy, exitSell, transactionModel, transactionModel). So we need to pass cost models as well. For null entry and exit, we can use new Position(null, null, transactionModel, transactionModel). However the class may not have such constructor; but given existing tests they used that signature. So we will use same.

For mock entry trade, we need to also pass transactionModel? Not needed for hashCode.
